research_rationale: EO 11992 (May 24, 1977; 42 FR 27195-27196, held official FR scan text) established the Committee on Selection of Federal Judicial Officers, an advisory committee under the Federal Advisory Committee Act. All fourteen operative clauses (Secs. 1-8, subsections separated) are quoted verbatim from the held OCR text. The order set its own end in Sec. 8 (termination on December 31, 1978 unless sooner extended); that end did not occur because EO 12110 (sec. 1-101(i), effective December 31, 1978) continued the Committee until December 31, 1980, and EO 12258 (sec. 1-101(g), effective December 31, 1980) continued it until December 31, 1982, so the chain is unbroken. Before that extended term ran out, EO 12305 of May 5, 1981 (46 FR 25421, item (b)) revoked EO 11992 and terminated the Committee; EO 12305 states no other effective date, so every clause's first end is May 5, 1981, which is also the whole-order end. No amendment of EO 11992 was found (OFR 1989 disposition table: 'Continued by EOs 12110, 12258; Revoked by EO 12305'; USC note at 28 U.S.C. pt. I agrees). The revocation leaves no savings or residual effect.

Sec. 3. Functions o f Panels, (a) A panel shall begin functioning when the  
President or his designee notifies its Chairman that the President desires the  
panel’s assistance in aid of his constitutional responsibility and discretion to  
select a nominee to fill a vacancy or vacancies on a United States Court of  
Appeals. Upon such notification, the panel shall:
(1) Give public notice of the vacancy or vacancies within the relevant  
geographic area, inviting suggestions as to potential nominees;
(2) Conduct inquiries to identify potential nominees;
(3) Conduct inquiries to identify those persons among the potential nomi­
nees who are well qualified to serve as a United States Circuit Judge; and
(4) Report to the President, within the time specified in the notification of  
the vacancy or vacancies, the results of its activities, including its recommenda­
tions as to the persons whom the panel considers best qualified to fill the  
vacancy or vacancies.

the President the names of the persons it deems best qualified to fill an  
existing vacancy or vacancies, a panel shall have determined:
(1) That those persons are members in good standing of at least one state  
bar, or the District of Columbia bar, and members in good standing of any  
other bars of which they may be members;

States Circuit Judge.

research_rationale: PARTIAL. EO 8744 (April 24, 1941; 6 FR 2118-2119, held official FR scan text, closing tag '[No. 8744]') has a single operative paragraph: an incumbent of a position covered into the classified service by section 1 of EO 8743 who is involuntarily separated by reduction in force, abolition of the position or liquidation of the agency between the date of EO 8743 and the effective date of its section 1 may acquire a classified status for transfer, provided (among other things) that 'he obtains such transfer within one year from the date of his separation'. By its own terms the authorization could therefore operate only for separations up to the effective date of section 1 of EO 8743 (January 1, 1942 under EO 8743 Sec. 2, earlier for positions that fell vacant after June 30, 1941) and transfers within one year after them. The EO 12608 revocation of September 9, 1987 is a formal cleanup that follows this earlier cessation and is recorded as a later event, not the first end. The exact last day cannot yet be fixed: EO 8743 Sec. 2 was itself amended (EOs 9230, 9358, 9678, 9712 and others touch EO 8743) and it is not established whether any amendment moved the effective date of its section 1; and a transfer deadline is a condition of eligibility, so the date must be fixed from the text, not inferred.
